title: Wire a server to a route table
description:
Implement NewItemServer. It receives an address and returns a configured server value which is never started -- starting it is the caller's business.

Build the standard request router, register the routes below on it, and return a server that carries the address it was given and answers every request through that router.

The routes, each registered for exactly one request method:

- GET /items -> 200, body "item list"
- POST /items -> 201, and no body at all
- GET /items/42 -> 200, body "item 42". The id is not fixed: whatever single segment sits in that position is captured by the route and read back inside the handler, so GET /items/abc -> 200, body "item abc".
- GET /items/42/comments -> 200, body "comments 42". The same capture, one segment deeper.
- GET / -> 200, body "usage". This one answers the root and nothing beneath it.

Three further behaviours are checked, and you write no code for any of them. The router produces all three on its own -- but only if the routes above are registered precisely enough to let it:

- A path no route covers is reported as not found: GET /nope -> 404, and GET /items/42/extra -> 404. This is what anchoring the root route buys you; a root route written so that it also matches everything below the root would swallow both of these and answer "usage" instead.
- A path some route does cover, asked for with a method that route was not registered for, is reported as not allowed, and the reply carries a header listing the methods that would have been accepted: DELETE /items -> 405, allowed "GET, HEAD, POST", and DELETE /items/42 -> 405, allowed "GET, HEAD". You only get this by naming a method on every route; a route registered without one accepts every method and the wrong one reaches your handler instead.
- Registering a route for GET answers HEAD as well: HEAD /items/42 -> 200. That is why HEAD appears in both allowed lists above without your having registered it anywhere.

Bodies are compared exactly and none of them ends in a newline.
objective: Practice registering method-qualified routes with a captured path segment, anchoring the root so unknown paths are still reported as missing, and handing the finished router to a server value.

title: Mount one router inside another
description:
Implement NewAPIServer. It receives an address and returns a configured server value which is never started. It builds two routers and mounts one inside the other.

The inner router carries the api routes, written as though the api were the whole site -- its patterns say nothing about where it is going to be mounted. Both are registered for GET only:

- one item by id, capturing a single segment: /items/42 -> 200, body "item 42"
- one file by the entire remainder of the path, however many segments that turns out to be: /files/a/b.txt -> 200, body "file a/b.txt". The captured value holds every remaining segment joined by slashes and carries no leading slash of its own. It is allowed to be empty: /files/ -> 200, body "file ".

The outer router mounts the inner one beneath /api/ so that the whole subtree below it goes there, and separately answers GET /health -> 200, body "ok".

Mounting alone is not enough. The inner router matches against the whole path it is handed and knows nothing about the /api part, so unless that part is removed first the inner routes never match and every api request comes back not found. Wrap the inner router in the standard wrapper that trims a leading prefix off the request path before passing the request on. Mind the asymmetry: the pattern the inner router is mounted under ends in a slash, because it covers a subtree, while the prefix being trimmed away must not, so that what reaches the inner router still begins with a slash.

Asked through the outer router:

- GET /api/items/42 -> 200, body "item 42"
- GET /api/files/deep/nested/file.txt -> 200, body "file deep/nested/file.txt"
- GET /health -> 200, body "ok"
- GET /api -> 307, redirected to /api/. You write no code for this one: a request for the bare root of a mounted subtree, with no trailing slash, is redirected by the router itself.
- GET /api/nope -> 404, GET /api/items/42/extra -> 404, and GET /nope -> 404

Bodies are compared exactly and none of them ends in a newline.
objective: Practice mounting a sub-router under a subtree with its prefix trimmed off, capturing the whole remainder of a path in one route, and letting the router answer the bare mount root itself.
